source: Watermelon (ដំណាំ ឪឡឹក) cultivation factsheet, undated; source publisher not stated on the visible pages but the structure and layout are consistent with MAFF/GDA vegetable-crop factsheet series (elibrary.maff.gov.kh). Uploaded PDF, no cover page present.
text:
Watering should be done regularly through the growing season, adjusted to weather and soil moisture rather than on a strict fixed schedule; irrigation is generally reduced as fruit approaches maturity, since excess late-season watering can dilute fruit sugar content and delay ripening (irrigation is tapered starting roughly 15-18 days before harvest in some guidance from this source).

Water is typically applied by furrow irrigation between raised beds/rows so that moisture reaches the root zone without waterlogging the plant base, since watermelon roots are sensitive to standing water and waterlogged soil promotes root and stem diseases.

Field sanitation practices mentioned include removing and destroying old crop residues and diseased plant material from previous seasons before land preparation, rotating out of watermelon and related cucurbits after successive plantings, and avoiding reuse of soil that has shown disease problems in prior watermelon crops without an intervening rotation to a non-cucurbit crop.
